Blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, heart rate is 70 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 96% on room air
Jugular venous pressure is elevated at 10 cm H2O.
Cardiac auscultation reveals a holosystolic murmur best heard at the left lower sternal border that increases with inspiration.

- Chronic heart failure, NYHA Class III

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset, crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm beginning 45 minutes ago while resting

lines: Sudden-onset, crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm beginning 45 minutes ago while resting

The patient is a 70-year-old male with known ischemic cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction, status post myocardial infarction, and severe secondary tricuspid regurgitation who was previously evaluated in 2020 for progressive dyspnea and lower extremity edema.
He presents with sudden-onset, crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm that began 45 minutes ago while he was resting.
- Ischemic cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction
- Chronic heart failure, NYHA Class III
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 62, hypertension
- Mother: Stroke at age 70, type 2 diabetes mellitus
Smoking: Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 5 years ago.
Vital signs show a blood pressure of 85/50 mm Hg and heart rate of 112/min.
He appears pale and diaphoretic. Auscultation reveals crackles at the lung bases.
ECG reveals ST-segment elevations in leads V2–V5.
He is started on oxygen and IV access is established.

encounters.cc: Black discoloration on the tips of fingers on both hands while recovering from cardiogenic shock

lines: Black discoloration on the tips of fingers on both hands while recovering from cardiogenic shock

This 70-year-old man with ischemic cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction, chronic heart failure NYHA Class III, and severe secondary tricuspid regurgitation, previously evaluated in 2020 for progressive dyspnea and parapneumonic effusion, is admitted to the intensive care unit for management of cardiogenic shock in the setting of chronic heart failure and recent myocardial infarction.
He is currently on mechanical ventilation and an intra-aortic balloon pump has been placed.
Despite these measures, his blood pressure remains critically low, and he is started on a norepinephrine infusion.
Three days later, the nurse reports that the patient has developed black discoloration on the tips of his fingers on both hands.
- Ischemic cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction
- Chronic heart failure, NYHA Class III
His current medications include aspirin, atorvastatin, furosemide, and metoprolol.
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 62, hypertension
- Mother: Stroke at age 70, type 2 diabetes mellitus
Smoking: Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 5 years ago.
On examination, the patient's distal digits are cold, with clear demarcation between healthy tissue and the areas of black eschar.
Pulses are not palpable in the affected digits.
The remainder of the cardiovascular examination is unremarkable.

lines: Progressive bilateral hearing loss over the past two weeks following recent hospitalization
Patient with ischemic cardiomyopathy returns for hearing loss following recent hospitalization.
He denies any ear pain, discharge, or recent infections.
He was recently hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure and received intravenous furosemide.
- Ischemic cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction
- Chronic heart failure, NYHA Class III
His current medications include lisinopril, carvedilol, spironolactone, and furosemide.
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 62, hypertension
- Mother: Stroke at age 70, type 2 diabetes mellitus
Smoking: Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 5 years ago.
His blood pressure is 142/88 mmHg, heart rate is 78 bpm, and respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute.
Physical examination reveals bilateral decreased air entry at the lung bases and 2+ pitting edema in the lower extremities.
- Serum creatinine: 2.1 mg/dL (increased from baseline of 1.5 mg/dL)
